status_summary: The outbound-investment strand is the most advanced: the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, signed 2025-12-18, includes the COINS Act (Public Law 119-60, division H, title LXXXV, section 8521, codified at 50 U.S.C. 4581 and following), which codifies and broadens Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program, authorizes Treasury to prohibit covered transactions, defines countries of concern as China (including Hong Kong and Macau), Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela under the Maduro regime, and requires Treasury to issue notification regulations within 450 days of enactment (by 2027-03-13, computed) that amend or replace the existing rules at 31 CFR part 850, which stay in force until then. The 2025-02-21 America First Investment Policy memorandum said the administration would seek to strengthen CFIUS authority over greenfield investments, directed CFIUS and other tools against PRC-affiliated investment in strategic sectors, and called for time-limited mitigation steps instead of open-ended agreements for adversary-linked investors, and a Senate bill (S. 1388, introduced 2025-04-09 and shown on GovInfo bill status as referred to the Senate Banking Committee with no later action) would extend CFIUS review to certain greenfield investments, but no greenfield rule or enacted law was found. Treasury's other CFIUS step, a request for information published 2026-02-09 on a Known Investor Program, would give an expedited path to repeat foreign investors that can show distance from adversary countries and asks about mitigation and monitoring burdens; it proposes no penalty schedule (Inference: its streamlining aim differs from the Mandate's emphasis on stricter scrutiny). A published penalty schedule, a Defense Department co-chair role and an equal-voice rule were not found.

timeline.event: The America First Investment Policy memorandum directs a faster process for investors from allied and partner sources, says the administration will seek to strengthen CFIUS authority over greenfield investments, calls for mitigation consisting of concrete time-limited actions instead of open-ended agreements for adversary-linked investors, and directs a review of possible new or expanded limits on U.S. investment in Chinese sectors such as semiconductors, AI and quantum.

Senator Moreno introduces the PROTECT Act of 2025 (S. 1388), which would extend CFIUS jurisdiction to certain greenfield and brownfield investments by entities of countries of concern; read twice and referred to the Senate Banking Committee, and the GovInfo bill status shows no later action.

CFIUS begins a Known Investor Pilot Program with a sample of frequent repeat filers, who complete a voluntary extended questionnaire, after Treasury states in May 2025 its intent to create a Known Investor Program. (month only; first of month used)

President signs the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (Public Law 119-60), whose division H, title LXXXV (section 8521) contains the COINS Act: it makes the outbound investment program statutory (50 U.S.C. 4581 and following), defines countries of concern as China (including Hong Kong and Macau), Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela under the Maduro regime, and gives Treasury 450 days to issue notification regulations that amend or replace 31 CFR part 850; the existing rules stay in force until then. The addition of hypersonics and high-performance computing to the covered technologies is as summarized by Baker McKenzie.

timeline.event: At a House Financial Services subcommittee hearing, Treasury's Assistant Secretary for Investment Security said new outbound investment rules will have to be written under the COINS Act (as reported by the Coalition for a Prosperous America, which also argues CFIUS review is too lenient).

Treasury publishes a request for information (91 FR 5694) on a CFIUS Known Investor Program, an expedited track for repeat foreign filers with verifiable distance from adversary countries, and on other streamlining; it asks about mitigation and monitoring burdens, with comments due 2026-03-18. The document does not discuss greenfield investment, penalty schedules or a Defense Department role.

title: Refocus CFIUS on China, add greenfield review, and restrict U.S. investment in China
uncertainties: The COINS Act was read through the U.S. Code text on law.cornell.edu (50 U.S.C. 4581, 4582 and 4589, each added by Public Law 119-60, division H, title LXXXV, section 8521, 139 Stat. 1924 to 1931), a partly primary route; the enrolled NDAA on govinfo (Public Law 119-60, S. 1071, enacted 2025-12-18) is cut off before that title. Section 4589 lists the six countries of concern directly, section 4582 sets the 450-day regulation deadline (2027-03-13, computed), and a note to section 4581 (section 8505) says the title ceases to have effect seven years after enactment. Other subtitles define country of concern as China alone for their own purposes. The technology additions (hypersonics, high-performance computing) rest on law-firm summaries. The Federal Register check for the outbound rules (31 CFR part 850) found no documents since 2025-01-20, and the check for CFIUS documents (31 CFR part 800) found only the February 2026 request for information. Greenfield coverage, a penalty schedule, mitigation-monitoring rules and a Defense Department co-chair role were checked only through those documents and the secondary sources above, so developments in CFIUS practice (for example enforcement actions or penalty announcements) may exist that were not found. The Dechert page was undated in the copy read, so its 2026-01-01 date is approximate. The Coalition for a Prosperous America is an advocacy group. Update 2026-10-15: a Federal Register query for Treasury documents on outbound investment since 2026-01-01 returned no proposed outbound rule (only unrelated tax items), and the CFIUS Known Investor Program page lists no step after the February 2026 request for information. S. 1388 is known only from a tracker page (congress.gov could not be fetched), so its status needs a primary check; whether it is the same as the greenfield legislation the memorandum envisions is not established. No CFIUS annual report for 2026 was located. Update 2026-10-16: S. 1388 status is now confirmed on GovInfo bill status (latest action 2025-04-09, referral to committee). A Federal Register query for outbound investment documents since 2026-02-09 returned no Treasury outbound rule (only an unrelated Commerce notice and a FinCEN proposal), and a query for Treasury CFIUS documents since 2026-02-10 returned none. The CFIUS site lists a CY 2025 annual report to Congress (release dated August 2026); it reports 234 mitigation agreements under monitoring at year-end 2025 and 40 site visits, refers to existing penalty and enforcement guidelines without a new schedule, and was read only in part, so it is recorded here as context, not as a qualifying action. A law-firm note of 2026-01-16 records Treasury outbound FAQs of 2025-12-23 that state the existing rules remain in force until COINS Act regulations issue. The CFIUS Known Investor Program page still shows no step after the February 2026 request for information and a pilot continuing. The COINS Act title of the enrolled law was still not reached on govinfo at that point; see the U.S. Code reading above. Independent review 2026-10-16: GovInfo bill status for S. 1388 (PROTECT Act of 2025, Sen. Moreno, cosponsors Sens. Slotkin and Sheehy) shows only the 2025-04-09 introduction and referral to the Banking Committee. The CFIUS CY 2025 annual report confirms 234 mitigation agreements and conditions under monitoring at year-end 2025 and 40 site visits, refers penalty decisions to the existing Penalty and Enforcement Guidelines, describes the Known Investor pilot launched in 2025 and does not mention greenfield investments; the copy read carries no release date, so the August 2026 date rests on the CFIUS reports listing as read by the researcher.
